age.evidence: Long-Evans rats of both sexes were bred in house or purchased from Charles River Laboratories (CRL, Wilmington, MA) at 8 weeks of age.

sex.evidence: Rats ( n = 49, 24 males and 25 females) were pair-housed in same-sex pairs

dosing.evidence: Psilocybin ... and DOI ... were dissolved in saline to a concentration of 1 mg/ml ... All injections were intraperitoneal ... Saline, DOI or psilocybin were injected 20 min before behavioral testing. ... Treatments were not repeated in the same animals
DOI (1 mg/kg, i.p.) did not improve set-shifting performance (Fig. 4a, p = 0.112, n = 12)

handling.evidence: After acclimation and handling, animals were food restricted to 85-90% of their free-feeding weight before training on behavioral tasks began

group_housing.evidence: Rats (n = 49, 24 males and 25 females) were pair-housed in same-sex pairs

day_night_flipped.evidence: under a 12 h reverse light/dark cycle with lights off at 9:00 am. All behavioral tasks were conducted during the active dark phase.

assays.assay_description: Operant extradimensional set-shifting task with two nose-poke ports; rats switch between 'Light' and 'Side' rules, with uncued rule change after 10 consecutive correct responses. Sessions last until 4 rule sets are completed or 45 min elapse. Three baseline sessions vs. one treatment session (saline, psilocybin 1 mg/kg, DOI 1 mg/kg, ketanserin or SB242084 pretreatment + psilocybin/saline). Measures: trials to criterion, completed sets, fraction correct, response time, number/length of streaks, time to criterion per set, perseverative/regressive errors.

setup_habituation.evidence: not reported (training procedures in Supplementary Material)

setup_restrain.evidence: on each trial one of two nose-poke ports became illuminated. Rats were required to respond to one of the ports

food_restriction.evidence: animals were food restricted to 85 -90% of their free-feeding weight before training on behavioral tasks began

water_restriction.evidence: No water source described in the operant apparatus during sessions; not explicitly stated.

time_to_assay.evidence: Saline, DOI or psilocybin were injected 20 min before behavioral testing. Antagonist were injected 10 min before the main treatment (30 min prior to testing).

sample_size.evidence: Adult rats of both sexes (n = 35, 18 males and 17 females) were trained in the task ... PSI n = 15; SAL n = 14; DOI n = 12; KET + PSI n = 14; KET + SAL n = 11; SB + PSI n = 11; SB + SAL n = 11

outcomes.summary: Acute psilocybin (1 mg/kg) improved set-shifting, decreasing trials to criterion and producing fewer but longer streaks of correct responses, with slower response times; effect was blocked by ketanserin but not SB242084, and ketanserin alone also improved performance. DOI (1 mg/kg) impaired performance, reducing completed sets and fraction correct. No sex differences.
outcomes.statistics: Psilocybin: trials to criterion p = 0.0005 (Fig. 2a legend; p = 0.005 in text), paired t-test; completed sets p = 0.546; response time p = 0.008 (Wilcoxon); fraction correct p = 0.188; number of streaks p = 0.025; streak length p = 0.034/0.041; vs saline Dunnett p = 0.005. Saline: trials to criterion p = 0.703; sets p = 0.237; fraction correct p = 0.463. DOI: trials to criterion p = 0.112; completed sets p = 0.012; fraction correct p = 0.005; vs saline p = 0.013. KET+PSI: trials p = 0.231, sets p = 0.688, fraction correct p = 0.469; vs saline p = 0.431. KET+SAL: trials p = 0.026, sets p = 0.680, fraction correct p = 0.050; vs saline p = 0.0004. SB+PSI: trials p = 0.0322, sets p = 0.484, fraction correct p = 0.249; vs saline p = 0.010. SB+SAL: trials p = 0.062, sets p = 0.762, fraction correct p = 0.031; vs saline p = 0.999.
outcomes.evidence: Psilocybin (1 mg/kg, i.p.) improved performance on the set-shifting task, as indicated by a significant decrease in the average number of trials rats needed to reach criterion ... rats completed significantly fewer sets when treated with DOI compared to the baseline period (Fig. 4b, p = 0.012) ... data for both sexes were combined as no sex differences were found

B1_num_measures.evidence: trials to criterion, number of completed sets, fraction of correct responses, response time, number of streaks, average streak length, time to criterion for each set, perseverative and regressive errors (Supplementary Table S1)

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: the effect of psilocybin on trials to criterion was most pronounced in the first two sets (Supplementary Fig. S2a), possibly due to it wearing off in sets 3 and 4 ... we computed the time to criterion for each set

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: Streaks (bouts of consecutive correct responses) are summarised as counts/lengths; no analysis of transitions between behaviours or sequences.

B5_social.evidence: Non-social operant task, animals tested individually.

B6_cognitive.evidence: set-shifting task, which tests an animal's ability to modify behavior, among competing and previously learned strategies

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Behaviour recorded as nose-poke responses; no pose estimation or ML classification.

B8_multivariate.evidence: t-tests, sign-rank tests and two-way ANOVA only.

E2_shelter.evidence: No shelter described in operant apparatus.

E3_bedding.evidence: No bedding described in operant apparatus.

E6_spatial.evidence: Single operant chamber with two nose-poke ports; ports are not separate compartments.

E7_social_context.evidence: Rats tested individually in the operant task.

E8_food_water.evidence: No freely accessible food/water in apparatus described.

D1_continuity.evidence: we calculated trials to criterion, number of completed sets, and fraction of correct responses, for 3 days of baseline and for the drug treatment session

D2_session_duration.evidence: Each session lasted until criterion was reached on four rule sets, or until 45 min elapsed.

D3_recording_days.evidence: 3 days of baseline and for the drug treatment session

D4_baseline.evidence: Three sessions of stable behavior were used as a baseline for each animal.

D5_followup.evidence: Only the acute treatment session (20 min post-injection) analysed; no post-drug follow-up data reported.

assays.assay_description: Pavlovian reversal task: two CSs (tone or flashing light) paired with food reward or mild foot-shock, 50 pairings per CS-US type per session across 10 sessions; contingencies reversed on session 6, when psilocybin (1 mg/kg) or saline was given 20 min before the session. Measure: R-value (food-port responding during cue vs ITI) per cue, across sessions and early vs late trials within the reversal session.

setup_restrain.evidence: R-value ... total number of responses in the food port during the cue presentations (animals freely approach food port)

food_restriction.evidence: animals were food restricted to 85 -90% of their free-feeding weight before training on behavioral tasks began

water_restriction.evidence: No water source described in apparatus; not explicitly stated.

time_to_assay.evidence: Injections of psilocybin (1 mg/kg) or an equivalent volume of saline were given 20 min before starting the task on the reversal session (session 6).

sample_size.evidence: Rats were injected with psilocybin (1 mg/kg, n = 7, 3 males and 4 females) or an equivalent volume of saline ( n = 6, 3 of each sex)

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin (1 mg/kg) given before the reversal session did not affect Pavlovian reversal learning for either the initially appetitive or initially aversive cue; both groups reversed similarly, and within-session learning did not differ between groups.
outcomes.statistics: Appetitive cue: mixed-effects main effect of Treatment p = 0.472; Session x Treatment p = 0.179. Aversive cue: Treatment p = 0.834; Session x Treatment p = 0.993. Within-session (session 6) appetitive: Timepoint p = 0.009; Treatment x Timepoint p = 0.487. Aversive: Timepoint p = 0.371; Treatment x Timepoint p = 0.754.
outcomes.evidence: No differences were found when comparing responses to each contingency pairing for the two treatment groups (Fig. 3c, d).

B1_num_measures.evidence: R-value computed for each stimulus (initially appetitive and initially aversive cue) in a session

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: we plotted the R-value in early (first 10) and late (last 10) trials in that session, for each animal, cue type and treatment group

B6_cognitive.evidence: reversal learning involves updating cue-outcome (or action-outcome) associations

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Food-port entries recorded; no behavioural classification software.

B8_multivariate.evidence: Mixed-effects model and two-way ANOVA only.

E1_environment_type.evidence: previously characterized task [32] with tone/light cues, food port and foot-shock

E6_spatial.evidence: Single conditioning chamber; no compartments described.

E8_food_water.evidence: Food delivered only as CS-contingent US; no free access described.

D1_continuity.evidence: Animals performed ten task sessions; R-values reported across sessions (Fig. 3c, d).

D3_recording_days.evidence: Animals performed ten task sessions ... Drug-naive and untrained rats were exposed to two different cue-stimulus pairings over 10 task sessions.

D4_baseline.evidence: On the sixth session, CS-US contingencies were reversed ... Injections ... given 20 min before starting the task on the reversal session (session 6); sessions 1-5 data reported.

D5_followup.evidence: Sessions 7-10 after the single psilocybin dose on session 6 were recorded and analysed (Fig. 3c, d, Session x Treatment).

judge_notes: Two assays retained (set-shifting, Pavlovian reversal learning); all candidates agreed. Antagonist and DOI arms collapsed into the single set-shifting assay per rubric.

Set-shifting B1 raised to 7+ (score 3): paper reports trials to criterion, completed sets, fraction correct, response time, number of streaks, streak length, time to criterion per set, and perseverative/regressive errors. Candidates' 4-6 undercounted; gemma's score 3 with value 4-6 was internally inconsistent.
Set-shifting B2 overridden to Yes (medium): paper analyses trials/time to criterion set-by-set within the session, attributing reduced effect in sets 3-4 to drug wearing off.
Set-shifting application_type set to i.p. (all injections intraperitoneal); gemma's 'multiple' rejected since only one route was used.
Set-shifting E6 = 0 (qwen's score 1 for two nose-poke ports rejected; ports are not separate compartments).
Reversal learning D3 set to 8-14 (10 sessions); deepseek counted 10 days but scored 2-7. D5 set to Yes since sessions 7-10 after the session-6 dose were reported (deepseek's reasoning).
Reversal learning B1 scored 1 (R-value for appetitive and aversive cues) matching modal score; qwen/gemma's value '1' with score 1 was inconsistent.
Food restriction coded 'before' per rubric example of pre-conditioning weight reduction for operant tasks; water restriction 'during' low confidence (not stated).
Handling coded 'yes' (medium): paper explicitly states 'After acclimation and handling', though no protocol details.
Fig. 2a legend reports p = 0.0005 while text reports p = 0.005 for psilocybin trials-to-criterion; both noted.
